","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"RESOLVED CO/92025/18 
Moved by Councillor Cr Janet Wilson, seconded by Councillor Cr Kieran Somerville
That Council:
  1. Receives and notes the report, Local Government NSW (LGNSW) Annual Conference.
  2. Nominates the Deputy Mayor as Council's voting delegate to the conference to be held 23-25 November 2025.
  3. Submits the following motions to be included in the LGNSW Annual Conference 2025 business paper:
  1. That LGNSW support the policy position, in conjunction with the current position of a 1% increase to federal Financial Assistance Grants, of removing the minimum per capita provision from the Financial Assistance Act 1985.
  2. That LGNSW launch a strong media campaign around its recently released cost shifting report to highlight the amount of additional regulatory and legislative costs councils are expected to absorb or services councils are required to deliver without supporting revenue from the other tiers of government.
  3. That LGNSW lobby the State Government for a Rural portfolio, separate to the Regional portfolio.
  4. That LGNSW lobby both the state and federal tiers of government to establish a dedicated Culvert and Causeway program, to better flood proof affected councils and repair a massive infrastructure backlog which directly relates to the 2022 floods and the floods caused by Cyclone Alfred.
  5. That LGNSW:
    - Run an education campaign around the Red Bench Initiative to encourage councils to roll out red benches, to raise awareness of domestic violence in their communities.
    - Encourage councils to join the Red Bench Initiative and begin to roll out red benches across their LGAs to create a unified position on domestic violence and be the first state, other than Queensland, to drive such a powerful message on domestic violence.
CARRIED
FOR VOTE - Unanimous vote

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"MOTION
Moved by Cr Janet Wilson, seconded by Cr John Burley
That Council:
  1. Receives and notes the report Determination of Development Application 2025/80 - Kyogle Memorial Recreation Centre
  2. Approves Development Application 2025/80 subject to the conditions stipulated in the assessment report.

Cr Brett McNamara sought to move the following as an amendment:
That Council defers consideration with respect to DA 2025/80 - Kyogle Memorial Recreation Centre subject to receiving the following:
A detailed Heritage Assessment to determine the heritage values of the Youthie Laneways Space building within the context of its interrelationship and as an element of Kyogle’s War Memorial.  This heritage assessment is to determine the buildings intrinsic heritage values and or associations with Kyogle’s War Memorial with respect to any applicable federal, state, or local heritage legislation and or planning instruments, policies, or controls.

The Mayor ruled the proposed amendment out of order as it did not amend the original motion and ruled that it would have to be a foreshadowed motion.

Cr Brett McNamara foreshadowed a motion:
That Council defers consideration with respect to Development Application 2025/80 - Kyogle Memorial Recreation Centre subject to receiving the following:
A detailed Heritage Assessment to determine the heritage values of the Youthie Laneways Space building within the context of its interrelationship and as an element of Kyogle’s War Memorial.  This heritage assessment is to determine the buildings intrinsic heritage values and or associations with Kyogle’s War Memorial with respect to any applicable federal, state, or local heritage legislation and or planning instruments, policies, or controls.

Cr Tom Cooper proposed the following amendment:
That Council does not approve DA 2025/80 - Kyogle Memorial Recreation Centre until there is a heritage assessment.

The Mayor ruled the amendment out of order as it was a direct negative of the original motion.

RESOLVED CO/112025/6 
Moved by Councillor Cr Janet Wilson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Cr John Burley
That Council:
  1. Receives and notes the report Determination of Development Application 2025/80 - Kyogle Memorial Recreation Centre
  2. Approves Development Application 2025/80 subject to the conditions stipulated in the assessment report.
CARRIED
FOR VOTE - Crs Danielle Mulholland, John Burley, Janet Wilson, Kieran Somerville, Robin Harley, Olivia Taylor, and Rob Cullen
AGAINST VOTE - Crs Brett McNamara and Tom Cooper

Cr Janet Wilson called for a division under Section 375A of the Local Government Act.

ForAgainst
Cr Danielle MulhollandCr Brett McNamara
Cr John BurleyCr Tom Cooper
Cr Janet Wilson
Cr Kieran Somerville
Cr Robin Harley
Cr Olivia Taylor
Cr Rob Cullen

As the original motion was adopted, the foreshadowed motion lapsed.

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Section 10A(4) of the Local Government Act, 1993 provides that members of the public are allowed to make representations to or at a meeting, before any part of the meeting is closed to the public, as to whether that part of the meeting should be closed.  Before closing the meeting, the Mayor asked the gallery if anyone would like to make representations to Council as to why the meeting should not be closed. No representations were made.

RESOLVED CO/122025/16 
Moved by Cr Janet Wilson, seconded by Cr Kieran Somerville
That Council considers the confidential report(s) listed below in a meeting closed to the public in accordance with Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993:

15.1 VISITOR INFORMATION CENTRE EXPRESSION OF INTEREST REASON FOR CONFIDENTIALITY The Council is satisfied that, pursuant to Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, the information to be received, discussed or considered in relation to this agenda item is: (d)(i) commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it.

15.2 LEGAL UPDATE REASON FOR CONFIDENTIALITY The Council is satisfied that, pursuant to Section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993, the information to be received, discussed or considered in relation to this agenda item is: (d)(i) commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it.

CARRIED
FOR VOTE - Unanimous vote

  1. Receives and notes the report Community Assistance Grants and Event Sponsorship Grants;

(a) $1,500 for the Kyogle Bazaar (Kyogle Christmas Markets) on the condition that the 2022 Flood Recovery Grant received is acquitted to Council satisfaction prior to the event on 13 December 2025.
(b) $5,000 for the Kyogle Progression Association (Summerland Giant Pumpkin and Watermelon Festival) on the condition that the 2022 Flood Recovery Grant received is acquitted to Council satisfaction prior to 15 December 2025.
(c) $2,000 for the Wiangaree Rodeo and Sports Organisation (Working Dog Trial) on the condition that the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development provides clearance for the event facility prior to the event.
 (d) $3,000 for the Bonalbo Progress Association (DogFest 2026) on the condition that the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development provides clearance for the event facility prior to the event.

CARRIED
FOR VOTE - Unanimous vote

[IGNORE_INDENT][OUTLINE_NUMBER_FULL_NO_PERIOD][AGENDA_ITEM_NAME]
","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"RESOLVED CO/122025/3 
Moved by Cr Tom Cooper, seconded by Cr Robin Harley
That Council:
1. Formally oppose the transition of the 176,000 ha of State Forest assessment area on the North Coast to National Parks and Wildlife.
2. Write to The Hon Chris Minns, Premier, The Hon Tara Moriarty, Minister for Forestry and local member The Hon Janelle Saffin, MP
3. Outlining how this transfer of forestry product will impact our local timber mills because much of the raw product comes from this area therefore putting local jobs at risk.
However, if the Government is intent on continuing down this path, Council 
  • seeks guarantees that effective land management resources and appropriate budgets be allocated for fire, pest and weed management programs in future years.
  • asserts that just and fair compensation be available for those directly and indirectly impacted by the closure of timber mills in our local government area.

CARRIED
FOR VOTE - Councillors Danielle Mulholland, John Burley, Brett McNamara, Olivia Taylor, Tom Cooper, Robert Cullen, and Robin Harley
AGAINST VOTE - Councillors Kieran Somerville and Janet Wilson

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"MOTION
Moved by Cr Brett McNamara, seconded by Cr Janet Wilson
That Council investigates the installation of an interactive heritage-based interpretive sign at Grove House. This interpretive sign is to pay homage to the building’s legacy as Kyogle’s Ambulance Station, acknowledging the pivotal role and history therein serving the local community.

AMENDMENT
Moved by Cr Janet Wilson, seconded by Cr John Burley
That the matter of historical signage for Grove House be referred to the Kyogle Historical Society (KHS) for consideration and or endorsement, of the proposal being put forward on the agenda, with a view to the KHS seeking grant funding if they believe that the proposal has merit, and inviting them to seek Council support in achieving an outcome.

CARRIED
FOR VOTE - Crs Danielle Mulholland, John Burley, Janet Wilson, and Kieran Somerville
AGAINST VOTE - Crs Brett McNamara, Tom Cooper, Rob Cullen, Robin Harley
ABSENT, DID NOT VOTE - Cr Olivia Taylor
With the votes tied at four all, the Mayor used her casting vote to carry the amendment.

The amendment became the motion.

RESOLVED CO/22026/4 
Moved by Cr Janet Wilson, seconded by Cr John Burley
That the matter of historical signage for Grove House be referred to the Kyogle Historical Society (KHS) for consideration and or endorsement, of the proposal being put forward on the agenda, with a view to the KHS seeking grant funding if they believe that the proposal has merit, and inviting them to seek Council support in achieving an outcome.
CARRIED
FOR VOTE - Unanimous vote
ABSENT, DID NOT VOTE - Cr Olivia Taylor

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"MOTION
Moved by Cr Janet Wilson, second by Cr John Burley
That Council:
  1. Receives and notes the report Request from Kyogle Museum to expand storage facilities on Council land.
  2. Endorses the following position:
    1. Kyogle Council provides the Kyogle Historical Society in principle support to pursue further development of Council land (Lot 207 DP4517) for the purpose of an additional storage facility for the Kyogle Museum, noting that any proposed development would be subject to development approval by Council and grant funding from external bodies.
    2. That Council does not support further development of Council land (Lot 207 DP4517) for the purpose of an additional storage facility for the Kyogle Museum.

AMENDMENT
Moved by Cr Janet Wilson, seconded by Cr John Burley
That Council support the museum in finding innovative solutions to the increasing pressure for storage so that the museum can develop an understanding of the status of the collection and subsets within the collection and how they can be managed for the future.
LOST
FOR VOTE - Cr John Burley, Cr Kieran Somerville, Cr Janet Wilson
AGAINST VOTE - Cr Danielle Mulholland, Cr Olivia Taylor, Cr Tom Cooper, Cr Robin Harley
ABSENT, DID NOT VOTE - Cr Rob Cullen and Cr Brett McNamara
The amendment was lost.

MOTION
Moved by Cr Janet Wilson, second by Cr Danielle Mulholland
That Council:
  1. Receives and notes the report Request from Kyogle Museum to expand storage facilities on Council land.
  2. Endorses the following position:
    1. That Council does not support further development of Council land (Lot 207 DP4517) for the purpose of an additional storage facility for the Kyogle Museum.

AMENDMENT
Moved by Cr Tom Cooper, seconded by Cr Olivia Taylor
That Council:
  1. Receives and notes the report Request from Kyogle Museum to expand storage facilities on Council land.
  2. Endorses the following position:
    1. Kyogle Council provides the Kyogle Historical Society in principle support to pursue further development of Council land (Lot 207 DP4517) for the purpose of an additional storage facility for the Kyogle Museum, noting that any proposed development would be subject to development approval by Council and grant funding from external bodies.

CARRIED
FOR VOTE - Cr Danielle Mulholland, Cr John Burley, Cr Kieran Somerville, Cr Olivia Taylor, Cr Tom Cooper, Cr Robin Harley
AGAINST VOTE - Cr Janet Wilson
ABSENT, DID NOT VOTE - Cr Rob Cullen, Cr Brett McNamara

Moved by Cr Danielle Mulholland, seconded by Cr Janet Wilson
That Council write to the NSW Government, the Queensland Government (via the Department of Transport and Main Roads, and Department of State Development, Infrastructure and Planning) and NSW TrainLink advocating for:
  1. An immediate review of the current XPT interstate passenger train timetable servicing Northern New South Wales and Brisbane, with a view to establishing more practical and accessible daytime services for residents, commuters, students, tourists and business travellers.
  2. The current review and development of rail service timetabling for the South-east Queensland rail network post commissioning of the Cross River Rail project, to include more practical and accessible daytime services for the XPT interstate passenger rail service, noting that additional network capacity will be available from 2029/2030 to enable this to occur.
  3. The Queensland Government to ensure that infrastructure to enable the XPT interstate passenger rail service to integrate with the Queensland Rail passenger rail network at Flagstone Central is included in rail corridor planning and detailed design for the Salisbury to Beaudesert rail line, scheduled to commence after the commissioning of Cross River Rail under the Queensland Government’s SEQ Rail Connect plan. Such an arrangement would provide improved connectivity, greater flexibility for travellers accessing destinations across the Brisbane metropolitan region, and more efficient utilisation of planned rail infrastructure and services. 
CARRIED
FOR VOTE - Unanimous vote

Moved by Cr Olivia Taylor, seconded by Cr Tom Cooper
That Council:
  1. Help promote community-based activities focused on food security, via social media and Council newsletter, to raise awareness about food security as a genuine and growing concern within our communities; and
  2. Engage with the community by conducting a community engagement program on the issue of food security, to bring community-based programs and community members together and to hear what our communities have to say.

AMENDMENT
Moved by Cr Danielle Mulholland, seconded by Cr Olivia Taylor
That Council:
 
  1. Help promote community-based activities focused on food security, via social media and Council newsletter, to raise awareness about food security as a genuine and growing concern within our communities; and
  2. Write to the NSW Government seeking implementation of Recommendation 6 of the Food Production and Supply in NSW Inquiry and Report (November 2022), namely that the NSW Government work with local councils to develop and implement strategies to improve local food systems and provide appropriate funding as required, and a timeframe within which this Recommendation will be delivered.
  3. That Council explore opportunities around the “Grow Local” program and how it can complement Council’s activities in the food security space.
 
CARRIED
FOR VOTE - Unanimous

The amendment became the motion.

RESOLVED CO/62026/9

  3. That Council explore opportunities around the “Grow Local” program and how it can complement Council’s activities in the food security space.
CARRIED
FOR VOTE - Unanimous vote

Moved by Cr Danielle Mulholland, seconded by Cr John Burley
That Council:
  1. Write to the Hon. Anthony Albanese MP, Prime Minister of Australia, the Hon. Chris Minns MP, Premier of New South Wales, Janelle Saffin MP Minister for Recovery and the North Coast, and Kevin Hogan MP, expressing the Kyogle LGA communities' strong objection to the proposed use of large-scale flood detention basins within the Kyogle Local Government Area as identified in the recent CSIRO report.
  2. Request that the evaluation and assessment and of any proposal involving detention basins within the Kyogle Local Government Area includes comprehensive consultation with potentially impacted landholders, local communities and Council, together with full public disclosure of the economic, environmental, social, infrastructure and agricultural risks and impacts, and construction costs.
  3. Advocate that any future flood mitigation investigations prioritise solutions that do not result in the permanent loss or significant impairment of prime agricultural land, rural communities, environmental assets or critical local infrastructure.
  4. That the $3 million feasibility study also look at nature-based solutions and other alternative solutions to the proposed detention basins.
     
CARRIED

  1. Write to the NSW Minister for Skills, TAFE and Tertiary Education requesting:
  1. The expansion of Mobile TAFE to deliver a broader range of vocational education and training courses directly within rural and remote communities including Kyogle where transport options and access to fixed TAFE campuses are limited.
  2. The development of Mobile TAFE courses in consultation with rural communities and local industries to ensure training reflects local workforce needs.
  3. TAFE NSW identify opportunities to deliver fee-free TAFE courses through Mobile TAFE, particularly where face-to-face attendance or practical components are required.
  4. The development of a place-based approach  to vocational education, recognising that simply making courses free does not remove the significant barriers faced by rural students when courses are delivered many hours from home.
  1. Advocate to the Australian Government for continued investment in fee-free TAFE and associated student support measures.
CARRIED
FOR VOTE - Unanimous vote

Moved by Cr Brett McNamara, seconded by Cr Olivia Taylor
That Council allocates $5,500 to support Kyogle Anti Violence Alliance (KAVA) & Kyogle Together Inc. ‘In Conversation with Ms Simone O’Brien: 16 Days of Activisms’ pending a detailed proposal from KAVA and Kyogle Together. Upon Council supporting and allocating the above funding, thereby creating planning certainty, KAVA will provide a program of events to Council.

AMENDMENT
Moved by Cr Mulholland, seconded by Cr Somerville
That Council defer the decision pending a detailed proposal.

Cr McNamara called a point of order saying the amendment did not meet the requirements of Section 10.11 of the Code of Meeting Practice in that the amendment did not relate to the original motion.
The Mayor did not uphold the point of order.

MOTION
Cr McNamara moved to dissent from the Mayor's ruling.

In accordance with Section 15.8 of the Code of Meeting Practice, the Mayor suspended debate on the Notice of Motion and called for a vote on the motion of dissent.
FOR VOTE - Crs McNamara, Taylor, Cullen
AGAINST VOTE - Crs Mulholland, Wilson, Somerville, Burley, Harley and Cooper.
The motion of dissent was lost.

AMENDMENT
Moved by Cr Oliva Taylor, seconded by Cr Robin Harley
That Council allocates $5,500 to support Kyogle Anti Violence Alliance (KAVA) & Kyogle Together Inc. ‘In Conversation with Ms Simone O’Brien: 16 Days of Activisms’  pending a detailed proposal from KAVA and Kyogle Together.

As the mover of the original motion, Cr McNamara said he was happy to accept the amendment as the motion.
Cr Mulholland withdrew her amendment.

RESOLVED CO/92026/5 
Moved by Cr Brett McNamara, seconded by Cr Olivia Taylor
That Council allocates $5,500 to support Kyogle Anti Violence Alliance (KAVA) & Kyogle Together Inc. ‘In Conversation with Ms Simone O’Brien: 16 Days of Activisms’  pending a detailed proposal from KAVA and Kyogle Together.
CARRIED
FOR VOTE - Unanimous vote

RESOLVED CO/92026/17 
Moved by Cr Danielle Mulholland, seconded by Cr John Burley
That Council:
  1. Receives and notes the report, Local Government NSW Annual Conference.
  2. Nominates Cr John Burley as Council's voting delegate to the conference to be held 22-24 November 2026.
  3. Submits the following motions to be included in the LGNSW Annual Conference 2026 Business Paper:
    1. That LGNSW campaigns the NSW Government to establish a dedicated whole-of-government Rural Portfolio to ensure the voices, interests and unique needs of rural and remote communities are represented in policy development, service delivery, funding allocation and strategic decision-making across all government agencies.
    2. That LGNSW, in partnership with the Australian Local Government Association (ALGA), advocate to the Australian Government for the number of Medicare-funded mental health support sessions available to people residing in Commonwealth or State disaster declared areas to be increased from 10 to 20 sessions for a period of two years following the declaration of a natural disaster.
    3. That LGNSW advocates to the NSW Government for the establishment of a dedicated Rural Roads Renewal Fund to upgrade rural, remote and regional roads, including unsealed roads, culverts and causeways, in recognition of their critical role in providing access for communities, emergency services, agriculture and industry.
    4. That LGNSW calls on the NSW Government to review the North Coast XPT timetable to improve connectivity between Grafton and South East Queensland, enabling residents to better access specialist medical services, employment, education, government services and family and social networks through improved integration with the South East Queensland public transport network.
CARRIED
FOR VOTE - Unanimous vote
ABSENT. DID NOT VOTE - Cr Wilson

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"RESOLVED CO/102026/2 
Moved by Cr Danielle Mulholland, seconded by Cr John Burley
That Council:
  1. Notes the increasing availability of AI-enabled smart glasses and other wearable devices capable of recording, processing and transmitting images, video and audio, and recognises the heightened privacy and child-safety expectations that apply in Council-operated toilets, change rooms, shower facilities, swimming-pool amenities, playgrounds, parks and recreation areas.
  2. Resolves to prohibit the unauthorised use of AI-enabled glasses, camera-equipped smart glasses and other wearable recording devices in Council-operated facilities and areas where heightened privacy protections are appropriate, except where consent has been obtained, the use is required for accessibility or disability support, is authorised for a legitimate operational purpose, or is otherwise authorised or required by law.
  3. Council investigate and implement appropriate amendments to relevant facility rules, conditions of entry and Council policies to give effect to this prohibition, ensuring that any proposed provisions appropriately balance privacy and child-safety considerations with Council’s obligations under applicable anti-discrimination and accessibility legislation.
  4. Council develops appropriate signage and community education measures to clearly communicate Council’s requirements regarding smart glasses and other wearable recording devices, and to report back to Council on the proposed amendments, implementation measures and any relevant legislative or regulatory considerations.
CARRIED
FOR VOTE - Unanimous vote
